Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an affair, and Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation.

In a memo to staff that Nvidia posted publicly, Huang wrote: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did."

The board says its inquiry follows reports that Huang was "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". According to The New York Times, the relationship was with an executive at an Nvidia customer whom US intelligence officials believed was working for the Chinese government. China's foreign ministry called that "purely groundless speculation".

The board says it has "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised" and that it has confidence in Huang. Nvidia says he will keep leading the company without interruption.

The stock traded at about $180.30 out of hours on Monday, around 3.4% below Friday's $186.64 close (Reuters). It was already 22% below its 6 October high of $239.24. Third-quarter results are due on 17 November.

Sources: Nvidia Newsroom, SF Standard, The New York Times, CNN, Reuters, Yahoo Finance. Photo: Anderseidesvik, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

The US economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, up from 2.2% in the second, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis advance estimate released on 29 October.

That is the fastest pace since the third quarter of 2025, and it beat the 3.1% economists had forecast (BEA, Yahoo Finance).

Consumer spending rose at a 3.8% pace and business investment excluding housing jumped 12.7%, with information processing equipment up 37.4% as the AI build-out continues. Housing investment fell 3.3% (AP).

Inflation cooled in the quarter: the PCE price index rose 2.1%, down from 5.0% in the second quarter (BEA).

This is the first of three estimates. The second is due on 25 November, and early GDP figures are often revised. The report came out five days before the 3 November midterm elections.

Sources: BEA, AP, Yahoo Finance. Photo: Architect of the Capitol, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

Not investment advice. CFDs are high-risk; you may lose money.
